titre: Cleft sentences (What I need is…, It was … that)
intro: “It was Awa who won”, “What I need is a holiday”: a cleft sentence splits one idea into two clauses to put one part in the spotlight. English has two main structures, “It is / was … that / who” and “What … is …”. They help you correct, contrast and highlight what matters, in speech and in writing.
objectifs: Make an it-cleft to highlight a subject, an object or a circumstance.
Make a what-cleft (What I need is…, What happened was…), including with a verb (What I did was call…).
Use the variants: All I want is…, The reason why…, The thing that…, That's what…
Avoid common errors (“What I need, it's…”, “It's in 2010 that…”).

sections.titre: What is a cleft sentence for?
texte: A cleft sentence divides one idea into two clauses so that one element stands out: you correct a mistake, contrast two things or build up to the important information.
Compare: “Marie sent the email” (neutral); “It was Marie who sent the email” (Marie, not someone else); “What Marie sent was an email” (an email, not a letter).
In speech, English often highlights with the voice alone: “MARIE sent the email.” Some languages use cleft structures much more often than English, so don't overuse them.
exemples: It was Marie who sent the email, not Paul.
Highlighting the subject, contrast.
What surprised me was his reaction.
Delaying the key information to make it stand out.
MARIE sent it.
In speech, stress is often enough.

sections.titre: It-clefts: It is / was + element + that / who
texte: Structure: It + be + highlighted element + that / who + rest of the sentence. Use “who” for a person (“that” is also possible) and “that” for everything else. Avoid “which” here.
You can highlight a subject, an object or a circumstance (place, time, reason), but not the verb itself.
The tense of “be” usually follows the tense of the sentence: past → “It was”. Say “It was in 2010 that I moved”, not “It's in 2010 that I moved”.
Negative and contrast: “It wasn't the price that worried me, it was the delay.” With a personal pronoun, everyday English says “It was me who…”; “It was I who…” is very formal.

lignes: It was Awa who won the prize.
It was my keys that I lost (not my wallet).
It was in Brussels that we met.
She left because of the noise.
It was because of the noise that she left.
It's the delay that worries me.

texte: Structure: What + subject + verb + be + highlighted element. “What” means “the thing that”. The important information comes at the end, after “is / was”.
To highlight an action, use “do”: “What I did was (to) call the police.” After “was”, use the base form, with or without “to”.
To tell a story: “What happened was (that) the train broke down.”
You can reverse the order: “A holiday is what I need.” “That's what I mean.” “That's what I said!”
exemples: What I need is a long holiday.
The key information comes last.
What worries me is the cost.
What + verb (as subject).
What I did was (to) call the bank immediately.
Highlighting an action.
What happened was that the train broke down near Namur.
Introducing a story.
Patience is what you need.
Reversed order.

texte: Other words can replace “What”: All (= the only thing), The thing (that), The reason (why), The place (where), The person (who), The day (when), The only thing.
“All I want is…” is very common and means “I only want…”: “All I want is some peace and quiet.”
“The reason why… is that…”: avoid “the reason is because” in careful writing, as it repeats the idea.

lignes: All I want is to sleep.
The thing I love about Montreal is the festivals.
The reason why I left is that I was bored.
The place where we met was a café in Liège.
The person who helped me most was my aunt.
The only thing I regret is not learning sooner.

sections.titre: Agreement, punctuation and errors to avoid
texte: After a what-cleft, “be” is usually singular, even when the element is plural: “What we need is more teachers.” (“are” is possible but less common.)
No comma and no extra “it”: “What I need is a coffee”, never “What I need, it's a coffee”.
Don't combine “what” with another noun: “The thing what I like” is wrong; say “The thing (that) I like” or “What I like”.
exemples: What we need is more volunteers.
Singular “is” even with a plural.
What I love about Dakar is the ocean.
No comma, no “it”.
It's not that I don't like you, it's just that I'm tired.
Common expression to explain gently.

formule: It is / was + element + that / who … · What + subject + verb + is / was + element
prononciation: The main stress falls on the highlighted element: “It was AWA who won”, “What I need is a HOLiday”.
In an it-cleft, “It was” and “that” are weak: /ɪt wəz ˈɑːwə ðət ˈwʌn/.
In a what-cleft, the first part often has a rising or level tone, then the voice falls on the element: “What I need ↗ is a holiday ↘”.
“What I did was call…”: a short pause after “was” can build suspense.
In writing, cleft sentences replace spoken stress; that is why they are common in argumentative texts.
erreurs: What I need, it's a holiday.
What I need is a holiday.
No comma and no extra “it”.
It's in 2015 that I moved to Douala.
It was in 2015 that I moved to Douala.
Past event: “It was”.
It was my sister which told me.
It was my sister who (that) told me.
For a person: who or that.
What I did was I called the police.
What I did was (to) call the police.
After “What I did was”: base form.
The thing what annoys me is the noise.
The thing that annoys me (What annoys me) is the noise.
Don't combine “the thing” and “what”.
That I like is the food.
What I like is the food.
The cleft starts with “What”, not “That”.
The reason is because I was tired.
The reason (why I left) is that I was tired.
Careful writing: the reason… is that.

dialogue.contexte: In Ottawa, Jonathan and Sabrina have a friendly argument after finding their restaurant closed on their wedding anniversary.
lignes: I can't believe it. You forgot to book the table!
Wait. It wasn't me who was supposed to book. It was you!
No. What I said was that I would choose the restaurant, not book it.
OK, maybe. But what really annoys me is that they close on Mondays and nobody told us.
It's not that I'm angry. It's just that I was really looking forward to it.
It's not that…, it's just that…
I know. So what I suggest is this: we buy some poutine and eat it by the canal.
What I suggest is this: introduces a proposal.
Poutine on our anniversary? Well, that's what we ate on our first date…
Exactly. All I want is to spend the evening with you.

mots: The focus of the sentence is the price.
She emphasised the need for patience.
to show that something is important (US: emphasize)
the main idea in an argument
What matters is that you're safe.
What annoys me is the noise.
to make someone a little angry
The reason why I called is that I need help.
a situation where people don't understand each other correctly
Let me clarify what I meant.
I was really looking forward to the trip.
to feel happy about something that will happen

exercices.consigne: Which element does the sentence highlight?
items: What I need is a long holiday.
a long holiday
It was in Brussels that we met.
in Brussels (the place)
All I want is some peace and quiet.
some peace and quiet
It's the price that worries me.
the price

exercices.consigne: Complete with one word: it, what, that, who or is.
items: ___ was my brother who told me the news.
It
___ I like most about Montreal is the festivals.
What
It was in 2019 ___ she started her company.
that
What we need ___ more time.
is
It was the manager ___ made the decision.
who (or that)
___ I did was call the bank immediately.
What

exercices.consigne: Rewrite starting with the word given, to highlight the element indicated.
items: Paul broke the window. (It…; Paul)
It was Paul who (that) broke the window.
I need a good night's sleep. (What…)
What I need is a good night's sleep.
We met in Dakar. (It…; Dakar)
It was in Dakar that we met.
His attitude annoys me. (What…)
What annoys me is his attitude.
I only want to sleep. (All…)
All I want is to sleep. (or: All I want to do is sleep.)

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: What I need it's a coffee.
What I need is a coffee.
It's in 2010 that they got married.
It was in 2010 that they got married.
What I did was I called a taxi.
What I did was (to) call a taxi.
It was the neighbours which complained.
It was the neighbours who (that) complained.

exercices.consigne: Answer “No” and correct the information with an it-cleft, using the word in brackets.
items: “Tom sent the email, didn't he?” (Lisa)
No, it was Lisa who (that) sent the email.
“You met in Paris, right?” (Brussels)
No, it was in Brussels that we met.
“Does the noise bother you?” (the smell)
No, it's the smell that bothers me.
“You started your job in May?” (June)
No, it was in June that I started.

exercices.consigne: Describe your town or your job in 4 different cleft sentences: one with “It”, one with “What”, one with “All” and one with “The thing / The reason”.
items: Example answer

It was in 2018 that I moved to Liège for my studies. What I love about the city is its friendly atmosphere. All I miss is the sun of my home town. The reason why I stayed is that I found a great job here.

a_retenir: It is / was + element + that / who…: highlights a subject, object or circumstance.
Past tense → “It was”: It was in 2010 that…
What + subject + verb + is + element: What I need is…, What I did was (to) call…, What happened was that…
Variants: All I want is…, The thing (that)…, The reason why… is that…, That's what…
Never “What I need, it's…”; English uses fewer clefts than some languages and often uses stress instead.
